sessions.title: Distinguish a negative verb from a negative noun predicate

steps.title: A speaking reply and its negative
steps.body: Да, говорю́ — Yes, I'm speaking. Нет, не говорю́ — No, I'm not speaking. The first word of each reply answers yes or no. The separate negative particle before the speaking verb negates that predicate; it is not merely the initial no reply. The guided choice keeps the speaking action and changes it to a negative reply.

steps.title: A verb and a zero present copula
steps.body: To negate a verb, simply add не (nye) before the verb: the shown examples illustrate this ordinary predicate-negation pattern. In a present-tense noun predicate, the verb corresponding to is is normally omitted. The negative particle can then stand before the noun predicate itself. That is a different structure from a speaking verb with a negative particle.

steps.title: The question and the student statement
steps.body: Вы говори́те? — Are you speaking? Он не студент — He's not a student. The speaking question is not itself negated. The student statement has a noun predicate and no overt present-tense is. The check asks for that negative nominal sentence, not another speaking reply.

steps.title: A complete negative coming sentence
steps.body: Борис не приходит — Boris isn't coming. The negative particle precedes the coming verb. This complete sentence identifies Boris as the subject and coming as the action. The options не студент and не говорю́ are shorter fragments about being a student or speaking; they do not express the complete Boris-coming sentence. These choices recognize supplied structures rather than independently constructing every negative predicate.

sessions.title: Distinguish existence, absence and the negative particle

steps.title: Existence and absence are not yes and no replies
steps.body: есть means exists in the supplied existence pattern. нет expresses absence in its negative counterpart. The same word can also be a no reply, but that conversational use is different from the absence construction. Да is a yes reply. The separate particle не negates a predicate; it is not the standalone replacement for existence in this pattern.

steps.title: The noun after the absence construction
steps.body: If it isn't there, we use нет followed by the genitive. In this construction the person or thing whose existence or possession is denied is expressed in the genitive. Do not replace the existence word with the separate particle and leave the construction unchanged. The checks identify the supplied existence/absence forms, not independently produce a genitive noun phrase.

steps.title: A pronunciation label is not a translation
steps.body: не — nye in the retained example is a pronunciation/transliteration label, not an English meaning. This particle is different from нет expressing absence and from есть asserting existence. A reference cue can be shown while the question asks for a contrasting form; read whether the question asks for existence, absence or ordinary predicate negation.

sessions.title: Keep noun number and case distinct under negation

steps.title: The singular and plural examples used by the checks
steps.body: Я не ви́жу э́ту кни́гу. — I don't see this book, singular. Я не ви́жу кни́гу — I don't see the book. Я не ви́жу книг. — I don't see any books. The first two show a singular accusative object; the last shows a genitive plural object. Negation remains in every sentence. Changing noun form does not turn the statement into a positive one.

steps.title: Genitive is not simply a plural marker
steps.body: A negated direct object can be genitive or accusative depending on meaning, context and usage. Indefinite reference often favors genitive, but this is not a mechanical rule that every negative sentence must use it. The older book ending in the retained source can also be genitive singular or accusative plural; it is not unambiguous genitive plural. The worked example now uses the same explicit plural-genitive phrase as the repaired check. I don't see the one book is still a singular description. I see this book and I see the books are positive descriptions and therefore do not match the negated cues. These choices distinguish supplied meanings and number, not independently choose every case under negation.

sessions.title: Distinguish negative pronouns from absence and indefinite forms

steps.title: Nobody and nothing refer to different categories
steps.body: кто — никто́. что — ничто́. The first pair concerns a person and nobody; the second concerns a thing and nothing. The indefinite options не́кто and не́что refer to an unspecified person or thing, not the corresponding nobody/nothing form. Do not treat a similar-looking prefix as proof of the same meaning.

steps.title: No person available for an action
steps.body: Negative predicative constructions express the absence of a person or thing for an action. The construction selects a case form; it has no nominative form. Compare the indefinite pronoun separately. не́кого спросить — there is nobody to ask. This is absence of a person available for the infinitive action; it differs from an unspecified person and from there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: The case comes from the construction
steps.body: не́кто is an indefinite pronoun, a person whose identity is not specified. It is not the predicative negative of кто. Absence of a person uses a case form: не́кого has the same form in the genitive and accusative, while не́кому is dative and не́кем instrumental. The sentence determines the case; absence meaning alone does not. There is no nominative form in this negative paradigm. The current checks recognize the absence meaning; they do not uniquely identify genitive from the shared genitive/accusative form.

sessions.title: Combine negative pronouns with the predicate particle

steps.title: One negative meaning across pronoun and predicate
steps.body: никто́ — не. ничто́ — не. In the supplied negative-concord pattern, the negative pronoun requires the separate negative particle in the predicate. They work together to express one overall negative statement. Do not remove the predicate particle by applying the English idea that two negatives must cancel.

steps.title: A prefix and a whole pronoun are not the predicate particle
steps.body: The option ни- is a pronoun prefix, not the separate predicate particle. никому is a declined pronoun referring to nobody in the dative; it is not that particle either. The answer не is the required predicate particle in the illustrated pattern. The choices recognize this supplied concord rule; they do not test producing every negative pronoun case or all exceptional constructions.

sessions.title: Interpret the supplied readings in stated contexts

steps.title: Two supplied readings with their stated contexts
steps.body: Не надо меня уговаривать. — One should not persuade me in the supplied context where the speaker would never agree. Меня не надо уговаривать. — There is no need to persuade me in the supplied context where the speaker will do it anyway. The questions provide these contexts rather than asking you to infer one unique interpretation from word order alone.

steps.title: Word order is not a universal meaning switch
steps.body: Word order can change what is in focus or in the scope of a particle. It does not by itself assign one unique meaning to every sentence. Intonation and discourse context matter as well. The current source illustrates these two contextual readings; a speaker could use a sentence with a different intended emphasis in another context. The checks recognize the supplied reading, not a universal rule that moving the subject always changes prohibition into lack of necessity.

steps.title: Use context to identify the supplied emphasis
steps.body: В магазин пошёл я. — It was me who went to the shop. In this supplied example the person who went is highlighted. Compare В магазин я пошёл. — To the shop—that's where I went. in the source’s destination-response context. Guided practice uses the highlighted-person example, with a different complete sentence and requested information from either independent persuasion check. The independent requirements still test both original persuasion contexts:the speaker will do it anyway, or the speaker would never agree. Subject-focus remains introductory guided evidence, not an independently demonstrated skill. Intonation and discourse context can affect readings; these examples do not establish a universal word-order switch or permission to infer present time from a past verb. sessions.title: Distinguish negating the state from negating its experiencer

steps.title: Not cold and not me are different scopes
steps.body: Мне не холодно. — To me it is not cold. This can also be expressed in English as I am not cold. Не мне холодно. — It is not to me that it is cold. The first negates the cold state for the experiencer; the second contrasts the experiencer, so the person who is cold is not me. The second does not by itself identify that other person.

steps.title: Use the demonstrated contrast with its limits
steps.body: Note that the modifier не negates the word which comes right after it. In this supplied pair, its position helps distinguish the state from the experiencer. Wider sentences also depend on construction, emphasis and context; do not apply adjacency as an automatic complete interpretation of every Russian sentence. The check asks for the scope shown in this pair, not free production of every negative-focus construction.

sessions.title: Distinguish the parts of a Russian personal name

steps.title: First name, patronymic and family name
steps.body: имя means first name. отчество means patronymic name. фамилия means family name. A patronymic identifies the father-derived part of a name; it is not the family name. These labels identify three name components rather than three alternative words for the same component.

steps.title: A suffix is not a whole name category
steps.body: The retained introductory pattern describes a father's first name with ович, meaning son of, or овна, meaning daughter of. These are suffix labels, not whole words meaning first name, patronymic name or family name. They illustrate common patronymic patterns; they are not an exhaustive formation rule for every name.

steps.title: Read the two-part worked example
steps.body: Василий Иванович shows a first name followed by a patronymic. The surname is not shown. The older note For instance is a source fragment, not a translation of the name. A complete three-component name also has a family name. The choices recognize these components and do not ask you to construct a new patronymic.

sessions.title: Distinguish a request, thanks and an apology

steps.title: Request and thanks have different functions
steps.body: Пожа́луйста means please in the supplied request use. Спаси́бо means thanks or thank you. A request asks for something; thanks responds with gratitude. The checks use these functions rather than treating all courtesy words as interchangeable.

steps.title: An apology is not thanks
steps.body: Извини́те means excuse me with polite or plural address. Извини́ is the familiar singular form. In the checked descriptions, excuse me, polite or plural identifies the first form; excuse me, familiar singular identifies the second. Neither is the thank you response.

steps.title: Read the address distinction

steps.title: Explain the Russian classification labels
steps.body: Марюня is classified here as от полной формы имени, meaning from the full form of the name. Машенька is classified as от краткой формы, meaning from the short form. steps.title: Distinguish derivation from social coloring
steps.body: Сашка is classified in this material as оттенок пренебрежения, meaning a shade of dismissiveness. That label describes social coloring; the two labels about full and short forms describe derivational bases. A form can have a base and social coloring at the same time. The question asks for the classification documented for this example, not mutually exclusive properties of every name.

steps.title: Keep the coloring claim within its context
steps.body: The retained text associates diminutive forms with the suffix -к- with dismissive coloring. Treat this as the source's classification of its examples, not proof that every use of every such name is insulting. Relationship, tone and setting affect interpretation. A documented label does not authorize inventing a new personal-name form or addressing someone that way without regard to their preference.

steps.title: Full and short forms
steps.body: Ирина is classified as полные имена, meaning full names. Ира is classified as краткие имена, meaning short names. These are forms of the supplied personal name, not different family names. A category identifies the form; it does not by itself settle what is courteous in every conversation.

steps.title: An affectionate form is another category
steps.body: Ирочка is classified as уменьшительно-ласкательные, meaning diminutive or affectionate forms. The full-name category полные имена and the short-name category краткие имена differ from this affectionate category. The examples recognize conventional forms; they do not license mechanical suffix formation for an unfamiliar name.

steps.title: Read the supplied register example without overgeneralizing
steps.body: For address by полному имени, meaning the full name, the source describes отстранённо-официального регистра, a detached formal register. The check asks for the stated register, not every possible setting where a full name occurs. This example does not mean full first names are always formal, or that they always replace a patronymic in formal address. Relationship, setting and the person's preference matter.

sessions.title: Recognize documented name forms without inventing new ones

steps.title: Conventional forms have documented bases
steps.body: Familiar, short, affectionate, and diminutive personal-name forms are conventional and socially marked. Марюня is the supplied documented derivative of the full name; Машенька is the supplied documented derivative of the short form. These English descriptions classify the examples already studied. They are not instructions to create an unfamiliar name.

steps.title: Several forms and a stated coloring
steps.body: One personal name may have several documented forms. Сашка carries documented dismissive coloring in the supplied material. That description concerns social coloring, while documented derivative of the full name and documented derivative of the short form concern derivational bases. Tone and relationship can affect actual use; the classification does not prove every utterance is dismissive.

steps.title: Verify a form before treating it as acceptable
steps.body: A suffix may add affectionate, familiar, diminutive, or dismissive coloring, but it does not mechanically generate an acceptable form for every name. For an unstudied personal name, the checked answer is unsupported until a names dictionary documents that form. The alternative the suffix mechanically generates an acceptable name overclaims what a suffix rule establishes. These checks recognize documented classifications and the verification limit; they do not assess free productive name formation.
